name: Orbitrap (r-z, quadro-logarithmic) -- 10 mm outer, 3.5 kV
notes: Orbitrap, cylindrically symmetric, solved in r-z (x = trap axis, y = radius; the kernel carries full 3-D Cartesian state, so the orbital motion is real). Both electrodes are truncated equipotentials of the quadro-logarithmic field U = (k/2)(z^2 - (r^2-R2^2)/2 + Rm^2 ln(r/R2)): central spindle through (R1, 0) at -Vc, outer barrel through (R2, 0) at ground; each profile is sampled uniformly in z, the spindle closed to the axis (solid; the real electrode continues as its support shaft), the barrel closed as a 1.5 mm radial SHELL (WALL_MM -- the trap-side boundary, the only one the interior field sees, is the same equipotential). Operating point: R1 = 6 mm (named choice, 10-mm-family value), R2 = 10 mm and Vc = 3500 V (Grinfeld/Monastyrskiy/Makarov 2015, Fig. 3/4), Rm = sqrt(2)*R2 = 14.142 mm (named choice: Rm > R2 required for the barrel surface to close), truncation |z| <= 12 mm. Injection slot deliberately absent: this is the unperturbed trap; the paper's slot/deflector compensation study sits on top of it. Ideal-field axial frequency sqrt(qk/m): the deck's build tool prints it at the operating point. Default source: one m/z 500 ion born ON the populated orbit of the paper (r = 6.5 mm, axial offset 4.8 mm) at the circular-orbit KE, purely tangential -- it should orbit at constant r while oscillating axially at the harmonic frequency. UHV: collisions disabled.
